usageNotes: Triggers a Ceph OSD scrub to detect data inconsistencies; use deep scrub (deep=true) periodically to also verify stored checksums against on-disk data. The call returns null immediately — scrub progress is tracked via Ceph itself (e.g., `ceph pg dump` or the Proxmox Ceph dashboard), not via a UPID. The target node must be online and the OSD must be in an 'up' state for the scrub to proceed.

examples.summary: Trigger a deep scrub on OSD.3 via node pve1

tips: Normal scrubs verify object existence and metadata; deep scrubs additionally read and verify all object data checksums — they are more I/O intensive and take longer.
Scrub frequency is also controlled by Ceph's automatic scheduler (osd_scrub_min_interval / osd_scrub_max_interval); use this endpoint to force an immediate scrub outside of that schedule.
If the cluster is under heavy load, consider setting 'noscrub' or 'nodeep-scrub' flags via the Ceph CLI before triggering manual scrubs to control timing.
Requires the Sys.Modify privilege at the root ('/') level — API tokens must have this privilege explicitly granted.
